newsitem.title: INDIA: India's United Front begins oil price meeting.
newsitem.headline: India's United Front begins oil price meeting.

text.p: India's ruling United Front coalition on Monday started a meeting to discuss the possibility of raising the domestic prices of some petroleum products, alliance officials said.
At its last meeting in May, the 15-party centre-left coalition was unable to reach a consensus on whether to raise prices to plug a mounting oil pool account deficit.

Domestic oil firms were owed 155 billion rupees ($4.3 billion) at the end of March from the oil pool deficit, which represents the amount owed by the government to the companies for selling below market prices.
Earlier on Monday, the main communist parties, key partners in the United Front coalition, reiterated their opposition to any proposal to raise petroleum product prices.
Both Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram have argued that prices must be adjusted to curtail the oil pool deficit.

Last July the government raised the price of gasoline by 25 percent, and prices of high-speed diesel, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) for cooking, paraffin wax and fuel oil by 30 percent. It was forced to scale back the rise in diesel prices to 15 percent after nationwide protests.
